name: Empress Embedded Database
tagline: Veteran embedded SQL RDBMS for RTOS and Unix devices, still sold but with little visible development.
description: Empress grew out of the MISTRESS project at the University of Toronto in the late 1970s and became a full-featured embeddable SQL database for real-time and embedded systems, with ports to QNX, VxWorks, LynxOS, Solaris and Windows CE. It offers ACID transactions, a SQL engine and C/C++, ODBC and JDBC interfaces, and has been used in telecom, medical, automotive and defence equipment. Empress Software still sells it, but its last widely listed release is v10.20-H (2023) and its website's news section has not moved in years. Treat it as a product for maintaining existing embedded designs rather than starting new ones.
statusNote: Still offered by Empress Software, but the last listed release is v10.20-H (May 2023) and public product news has been static for years.

pricing.notes: OEM and runtime licensing by quote; evaluation SDKs have been offered.

strengths: Mature embedded SQL with ACID transactions
Ports to many RTOS and Unix variants (QNX, VxWorks, LynxOS, Solaris)
Long field history in telecom, medical and defence devices
weaknesses: Little visible development or community since the early 2010s
Superseded in most new designs by SQLite or RaimaDB
useCases: Maintaining existing embedded systems built on Empress
Legacy RTOS devices needing SQL storage
